question: 'Emblica officinalis', whose Indian local name is □( ), is used in the preparation of Chyavanaprash.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amla**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Amla** is commonly known as *Indian gooseberry*.
 
• It is rich in Vitamin C and is known for its numerous health benefits, including boosting the immune system and enhancing hair growth.
 
• Amla is a crucial ingredient in **Chyavanaprash**, a traditional Ayurvedic health supplement.
 
• The scientific name of Amla is **Emblica officinalis** or **Phyllanthus emblica**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chyavanaprash**

 
 
• It is an ancient Ayurvedic formulation that is believed to be a rejuvenative and immune-boosting supplement.
 
• Chyavanaprash contains a mixture of herbs, spices, and other natural ingredients, with Amla being one of its primary components.
 
• It is traditionally used to improve vitality, strength, and overall health.
 
• This herbal tonic is beneficial for respiratory health, digestion, and overall immunity.
 
 
 
• **Neem**
 
 
• Scientific name: **Azadirachta indica**
 
• Neem is known for its medicinal properties and is often used in traditional medicine for treating skin conditions, purifying the blood, and maintaining oral health.
 
 
 
• **Mahua**
 
 
• Scientific name: **Madhuca longifolia**
 
• Mahua is a tropical tree found in India and is known for its sweet flowers, which are used to produce a traditional alcoholic drink.
 
• It has various medicinal uses, including treating skin infections and enhancing wound healing.
 
 
 
• **Opium**
 
 
• Scientific name: **Papaver somniferum**
 
• Opium is a narcotic drug obtained from the poppy plant, and it has potent analgesic properties.
 
• It is used in the production of various pharmaceutical drugs like morphine and codeine.
 
• Due to its addictive nature, the use of opium is strictly regulated in many countries.
